comment: The corresponding source of every copyleft library this artifact carries, so a release can offer
it from the same place as the binary — LGPL-2.1 section 6(d) and the last paragraph of GPL-2.0
section 3, which say that offering equivalent access from the same designated place counts as
distributing the source. That option needs no interpretation, unlike 6(b), whose first condition
is a copy of the library already present on the user's computer.
sha256 is filled in only where upstream publishes one to check against. Where it is null the
archive is generated on request by a forge and is not reproducible byte for byte, so what proves
the download is the digest of the file actually attached, recorded in SHA256SUMS.txt and signed.

sources.name: vlc
sources.note: The NuGet package's fourth digit is its own packaging revision. libvlc.dll declares file version 3.0.23, and 3.0.23 is what VideoLAN publishes source for; there is no vlc-3.0.23.1.

sources.name: LibVLCSharp
sources.note: Generated by the forge from the 3.10.0 tag, so its bytes are not reproducible and there is no published digest to check against. Taken from the GitHub mirror because code.videolan.org answers an unauthenticated fetch with an anti-bot page — which the first run of this script downloaded, named LibVLCSharp-3.10.0.tar.gz, and would have attached to a release as source code.
